signals.entity: ECB Banking Supervision / SSM significant institutions
signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia, Slovakia
signals.signal: PRIMARY TEXT NOW OBTAINED. ECB letter SSM-2026-0301 (Claudia Buch, 07/07/2026, 'Addressing AI-enabled cybersecurity threats') requires every SSM significant institution to submit a comprehensive AI-cyber action plan to its Joint Supervisory Team by 31/10/2026. Annex 1 names six mandated focus areas: (1) prioritise protection of attack surfaces incl. accurate identification of ICT assets, third-party software and open-source components; (2) accelerate vulnerability and patch management at scale; (3) enhance monitoring, detection and AI-enabled defensive capabilities; (4) strengthen governance, funding, awareness training and SUPPLY CHAIN ASSURANCE — management bodies must assess whether current 'ICT budgeting, staffing, tooling and change capacity are sufficient'; (5) reinforce defence-in-depth and 'modernis[e] infrastructure by replacing or updating legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies'; (6) improve response/recovery and crisis management aligned with DORA. ECB will run a HORIZONTAL ANALYSIS of submitted plans and feed conclusions back to SIs. The letter confirms the annual IT Risk Questionnaire (ITRQ) collection moves from Sept-2026 to FEBRUARY 2027, and flags a SEPARATE forthcoming ECB letter on post-quantum cryptography ('must start now').
signals.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — letter SSM-2026-0301, Claudia Buch, 'Addressing AI-enabled cybersecurity threats' (PDF)
signals.implies: Hardest-dated DORA-adjacent spend trigger in the footprint. 'Legacy, unsupported or end-of-life technologies' maps directly to ageing ATM estates and unsupported ATM OS/middleware: NCR Atleos ATM refresh, x-core multivendor ATM software, ATM/device telemetry and monitoring for the mandated ICT asset inventory, managed/field services for patch-at-scale, INETCO transaction monitoring for detection, Thales HSM for the flagged post-quantum track. Named Printec reference customers that are SSM SIs and therefore in scope: Alpha Bank (GR), Bank of Cyprus (CY), Erste&Steiermarkische/Zagrebacka (HR), Erste Group and RBI (AT).
signals.likelihood: Very high — action plans are due 31/10/2026 and JSTs will monitor execution; procurement of remediation tooling and ATM/OS modernisation must be committed in the plan itself
signals.followup: Ask SSM-supervised Printec accounts (Alpha, BoC, Erste HR/AT, RBI) what their 31/10/2026 action plan commits on ATM/OS end-of-life replacement and asset inventory; pre-position an 'ICT asset inventory + patch-at-scale for self-service estate' offer before Feb-2027 ITRQ.

signals.signal: NEW LEGAL INSTRUMENT, NOT IN BASELINE. Warning of the ESRB of 25/06/2026 on systemic cyber risks stemming from frontier artificial intelligence models (ESRB/2026/3), published in the Official Journal C series on 16/07/2026 as C/2026/3795. It is a formal Art.16 ESRB-Regulation warning addressed to all EU institutions and Member States, and it independently RECORDS the ECB's 31/10/2026 action-plan deadline in EU official-journal text (recital 13). The ESRB escalated its systemic cyber risk assessment from 'elevated' to 'severe'. Operative text says current patching practice in the financial system is 'predominantly reactive' and may become insufficient; it identifies four weakened-resilience areas (time-to-patch, defender capability, concentration on few AI/cloud providers, authority capability). Footnote 11 explicitly directs authorities to existing TESTING FRAMEWORKS — TIBER, threat-led penetration testing (TLPT, the DORA Art.26-27 adversarial red-team test), advanced red teaming (ART) and cyber resilience stress testing (CyRST) — as the vehicles for reducing these asymmetries. ESRB will reassess each quarter at General Board level.
signals.source_name: Official Journal of the EU, C/2026/3795 — Warning of the European Systemic Risk Board of 25 June 2026 (ESRB/2026/3)
signals.implies: Gives the 31/10/2026 ECB deadline an OJ-published legal footing (upgrades the baseline's ECB-letter-only basis) and puts TLPT/TIBER scope expansion on the table for the next testing cycle. Sells: ATM/device telemetry and monitoring (asset visibility), managed/field services for accelerated patching of distributed self-service estates, physical+logical ATM security, INETCO for detection, and TLPT-scope readiness work on ATM/POS channels.
signals.likelihood: High — ESRB re-assesses quarterly and national macroprudential authorities in HR, SI, BG, GR, CY, RO must reflect it in their own policy stance
signals.followup: Track the next ESRB General Board quarterly risk assessment (Sept/Dec-2026) for escalation from Warning to Recommendation, which would carry 'comply or explain' force on national authorities.

signals.signal: NEW. ESA Statement JC 2026 25, 'Toward a consistent and risk-based approach for ICT risks from frontier AI models', published 31/07/2026 — the day BEFORE the baseline cut-off and absent from it. It is not new law but sets supervisory expectations under DORA: entities must run 'comprehensive and continuously updated inventories of all IT assets (including infrastructure, applications, data repositories, APIs, and AI/ML components)', classify by criticality, move monitoring 'from periodic to continuous', and it cites Article 10 of the RTS on the ICT risk-management framework as the basis for automated vulnerability scanning, patch management and DevSecOps. Para 10 is the CTPP-relevant part: the ESAs AS LEAD OVERSEERS have already run targeted engagement with designated critical ICT third-party providers, have fed the results into the ANNUAL RISK ASSESSMENT CYCLE and the prioritisation of the 2027 OVERSIGHT PLAN, and are embedding AI-related risk into the Oversight Examination Methodology through 2027. Builds on the European Commission's Action Plan on Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence of 07/07/2026 and on ENISA's frontier-AI recommendations.
signals.source_name: EBA/EIOPA/ESMA Joint Committee — JC 2026 25, ESA Statement on frontier AI models (PDF)
signals.implies: Extends the ECB's SI-only 31/10/2026 push to ALL DORA financial entities including less-significant banks and payment institutions in the EU-11 footprint (RO, HU, CZ, non-SSM). The mandated continuously-updated IT asset inventory covering infrastructure and APIs is exactly the gap in most banks' ATM/POS estates: sells ATM/device telemetry & monitoring, TMS for POS terminal estates (Verifone/Castles), x-core for multivendor ATM software visibility, and managed services for continuous rather than periodic monitoring.
signals.likelihood: High — national competent authorities are expected to align supervisory dialogue immediately
signals.followup: Watch for the ESAs' 2027 Oversight Plan publication (expected late 2026) and whether any Printec-relevant provider or a second CTPP designation round appears; check whether BNR, MNB and CNB-CZ issue matching national circulars.

signals.signal: NEW AND ABSENT FROM BASELINE. NBU Board Resolutions No. 70, No. 72 and No. 73, all of 30/06/2026, in force 01/07/2026, install a full third-party-risk-management regime — Ukraine's functional DORA/ICT-third-party mirror — across BANKS AND BANKING GROUPS (No.70, amending the Regulation on the organisation of the risk-management system in Ukrainian banks and banking groups), FINANCIAL PAYMENT SERVICE PROVIDERS (No.72, amending the authorisation Regulation No.217 of 07/10/2022 and the management-system Regulation No.123 of 10/10/2024) and INSURERS (No.73). The consultation deck (04/06/2026) shows the new defined terms: 'third-party risk', 'TPSP provider', 'critical service', 'critical contract', 'critical TPSP provider', 'supply chain', 'service concentration risk', 'fault tolerance' and 'n-th party'. Requirements: pre-contract due diligence and documented risk assessment before signing a critical contract, grounds for refusing to contract, continuous monitoring of provider compliance, business-continuity management taking third-party risk into account, and exit/termination plans. Legal basis stated by NBU: para 50 of the Memorandum on Economic and Financial Policies signed with the IMF on 13/02/2026, plus PSD2 Art.20 and the EBA draft third-party-risk Guidelines EBA/CP/2025/12 of 08/07/2025.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — 'Requirements established for third-party risk management for banks, payment service providers and insurers' (official news + Resolutions 70/72/73)
signals.implies: Ukrainian banks (PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine, OTP Ukraine, Ukrgasbank) must now inventory, risk-assess and continuously monitor every critical ICT/technology supplier — including ATM/recycler vendors and outsourced field-service providers. This RAISES the bar Printec must clear as an incumbent supplier (PrivatBank NCR recyclers) but also creates demand for auditable device telemetry/monitoring, formal SLA-backed managed & field services, and documented exit/continuity plans. Combines with NBU Resolution No.143 of 09/12/2025 whose transition period ends 13/12/2026.
signals.likelihood: High — already in force; NBU is an IMF structural-benchmark deliverable
signals.followup: Obtain the text of Resolution No.70 from zakon.rada.gov.ua to extract the transition deadline for re-papering EXISTING supplier contracts (NBU news says banks are given 'sufficient time' but does not state the date); confirm whether Printec's Ukrainian contracts qualify as 'critical contracts'.

signals.entity: European Commission / EUR-Lex — DORA subcontracting RTS
signals.signal: VERIFICATION DEBT CLOSED AT REGULATOR TIER. The DORA subcontracting RTS is Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/532 of 24/03/2025, made under DORA Art.30(5), specifying the elements a financial entity must determine and assess when SUBCONTRACTING ICT services that support critical or important functions. Confirmed on two regulator-tier pages that link the Official Journal text: ESMA's own DORA policy page (Level-2 list, Art.30.5 entry) and the Croatian National Bank's Croatian-language DORA page ('Uredba Komisije (EU) 2025/532 od 24. ozujka 2025. ... pri podugovaranju IKT usluga kojima se podupiru kljucne ili vazne funkcije' [Commission Regulation (EU) 2025/532 ... on subcontracting ICT services supporting critical or important functions]). It was published in the OJ on 02/07/2025 and entered into force 22/07/2025 (that 22/07 date remains press/tracker-sourced because eur-lex.europa.eu itself returned an HTTP 202 JavaScript bot-check on every route tried this run). Scope: proportionality and group application, pre-subcontracting due diligence and risk assessment, conditions for permitting subcontracting of critical/important functions, monitoring of the whole subcontracting chain and required contractual terms. [STANDING - dated 2025.]
signals.source_name: ESMA — Digital Operational Resilience Act (DORA) Level-2 policy page, Art.30.5 entry; corroborated by Hrvatska narodna banka, 'Digitalna operativna otpornost'
signals.implies: Drives the sub-supplier ('n-th party') columns every footprint bank must populate in its DORA Register of Information. Printec is a subcontracted ICT provider to several footprint banks (managed/field services, TMS, ATM software), so it must be able to furnish chain-of-subcontracting data, LEI, service-location and exit-plan evidence on demand. Failure to supply it is a live displacement risk on renewals.
signals.followup: OPERATOR: open the OJ PDF for CELEX 32025R0532 in a browser to quote the entry-into-force Article verbatim; then map Printec's own subcontractor chain (field-service partners, cloud, TMS hosting) against its due-diligence Annex so it can be handed to bank clients on request.

signals.entity: ESAs / all DORA financial entities — Register of Information
signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Greece, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia
signals.signal: BASELINE DATE CORRECTED. The baseline listed '31/12/2026 EU: DORA Register of Information annual submission cycle'. Against the primary EBA FAQ on reporting of the registers of information (v. 28/03/2025), 31/12/2026 is the REFERENCE DATE, not a submission deadline: 'From 2026 onwards, the deadline to the reporting of the registers by the competent authorities to the ESA is set to 31 March of each calendar year', with the reference date being '31 December of preceding year for the registers to be reported form 2026 onwards'. So the 2027 cycle is: snapshot as at 31/12/2026 -> financial entities submit to their national competent authority in Feb/Mar 2027 on each NCA's own earlier internal cut-off -> NCA forwards to the ESAs by 31/03/2027 -> ESA data-quality feedback in April 2027, corrected resubmissions by end-April. The 2026 cycle sets the observable footprint precedent: Bulgaria's Financial Supervision Commission (KFN) told supervised entities the ESA production environment was open 25/02/2026-31/03/2026, that registers filed after 31/03/2026 would NOT be accepted, that entity submissions to KFN were due 23/03/2026, and that corrected registers had to reach the ESAs by 30/04/2026. The register template is set by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956 (DORA Art.28(9)).
signals.source_name: EBA — 'DORA RoI reporting FAQ' (updated 28 March 2025), PDF; footprint precedent: Komisiya za finansov nadzor (BG), 'Srok za predostavyane na informatsionniya registar saglasno DORA' [Deadline for providing the information register under DORA]
signals.implies: Every footprint EU bank must be able to describe, by LEI and by function, each ICT contract that supports a critical or important function AND its subcontracting chain, as at 31/12/2026. For Printec this is a recurring commercial exposure and opportunity: as a supplier of ATM/POS managed services, TMS, x-core and monitoring it will be asked for register-grade data (LEI, service type per Annex III taxonomy, data-storage location, subcontractors, exit plan) in Q4-2026. Supplying a clean, pre-formatted register pack is a low-cost renewal defence; failing to supply it is the single most common trigger for a bank to re-tender an ICT service.
signals.followup: Build a standard 'DORA Register of Information data pack' for Printec's own entity and push it to every EU-footprint bank client during Q4-2026, before their Feb/Mar-2027 filing. Watch BNB, BNR, HNB, BoG, CBC, CNB-CZ, NBS-SK, Banka Slovenije, MNB and FMA/OeNB for their 2027 entity-level cut-off notices (expect Jan/Feb-2027 publication).

signals.entity: ESAs / national competent authorities — threat-led penetration testing (TLPT)
signals.country: Croatia, Greece, Cyprus, Bulgaria, Romania, Austria, Slovenia, Slovakia, Czech Republic, Hungary
signals.signal: TLPT LEGAL BASIS CONFIRMED FROM A FOOTPRINT REGULATOR. TLPT — threat-led penetration testing, a controlled adversary-simulation red-team exercise against a live production environment, mandated by DORA Articles 26-27 — is specified by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190 of 13/02/2025 (DORA Art.26(11)). The Croatian National Bank's own DORA page carries the full Croatian title, confirming it sets 'kriteriji za odredivanje koji su financijski subjekti duzni provoditi penetracijsko testiranje vodeno prijetnjama' [the criteria for determining which financial entities must carry out threat-led penetration testing], the requirements and standards for using INTERNAL testers, the requirements on scope, testing methodology and the approach to each test phase, results, closure and remediation, and the supervisory cooperation needed for MUTUAL RECOGNITION of tests across Member States. Designated entities must run a TLPT at least every three years, executed under the TIBER-EU framework. The ESRB warning ESRB/2026/3 (footnote 11) explicitly points authorities to TIBER, TLPT, advanced red teaming and cyber resilience stress testing as the levers for closing the frontier-AI defender gap, which makes an expansion of TLPT scope and scenario content the most likely next supervisory move.
signals.source_name: Hrvatska narodna banka — 'Digitalna operativna otpornost' (DORA regulatory framework page, listing Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/1190); corroborated on ESMA's DORA Level-2 page
signals.implies: TLPT scope is set at entity level by the competent authority and covers the critical/important functions END TO END — which for a retail bank pulls in the ATM channel, the card-acquiring and POS estate, and the terminal-management and monitoring layer. Printec is exposed as the operator of parts of that scope (x-core, TMS, telemetry, managed/field services) and must be contractually ready to support a client's red-team window. Sells: physical + logical ATM security hardening, INETCO transaction monitoring for detection coverage during the test, and remediation work after the test report. Mutual recognition means a group-level test at Erste, RBI, OTP, NLB or UniCredit can pull Printec-operated estates in several footprint countries into one test scope simultaneously.
signals.likelihood: High — three-year cycle from designation; footprint SSM banks are in the first cohort
signals.followup: Ask HNB, BNB, BoG, CBC and BNR which entities they have designated for TLPT and in which testing window; confirm whether Printec's contracts with designated banks contain the co-operation and disclosure clauses TLPT requires (RTS 2025/1190 needs third-party providers to participate in scope).

signals.signal: CONFIRMED AT PRIMARY SOURCE, SCOPE WIDER THAN BASELINE. The Bank of Albania's Supervisory Council, at its meeting of 01/07/2026, decided to 'Adopt the Regulation on "Digital Operational Resilience" AND approve amendments to the Regulation on "Use of Information and Communication Technology by entities licensed by the Bank of Albania"'. The baseline recorded only the first instrument; the paired amendment to the existing ICT-use regulation is new information and means BOTH the new resilience rulebook and the legacy ICT-use rules move together. BoA states the regulation responds to 'increasing information and communication technology (ICT) and cyber risks facing banks and other financial entities' and 'forms part of the ongoing alignment of the Bank of Albania's supervisory regulatory framework with the EU acquis, in line with the commitments undertaken as part of Albania's European Union integration process'. NOT YET VERIFIABLE: the regulation number and the application date (the baseline carries 01/07/2027) are NOT stated in the Supervisory Council decision text, and as at 27/08/2026 neither the new Digital Operational Resilience regulation nor the amended ICT-use regulation appears on the Bank of Albania's public 'Supervision regulations' index (which still tops out at Regulation 51/2024 on operational risk management). Treat 01/07/2027 as UNVERIFIED until the numbered regulation or the Fletorja Zyrtare publication is obtained. Same meeting also approved BoA joining the IMF's new Southeast Europe Technical Assistance Center (SEETAC), covering AL, BA, XK, ME, MK, RS — a regional channel through which the same resilience template is likely to propagate.
signals.source_name: Bank of Albania — 'Decisions by the Supervisory Council, 1 July 2026'
signals.implies: Albania's banks — OTP Bank Albania and Raiffeisen Bank Albania are named Printec accounts, alongside BKT, Credins, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Albania, Tirana Bank and Union Bank — will have to evidence ICT asset inventories, third-party/outsourcing registers, incident classification and resilience testing on a DORA-shaped template. Sells: ATM/device telemetry & monitoring, x-core multivendor ATM software (visibility and patchability across mixed estates), managed/field services with auditable SLAs, and physical ATM security. If the application date is indeed 01/07/2027, BUDGET MUST COMMIT IN THE 2027 PLANNING ROUND, i.e. Q3-Q4 2026.
signals.likelihood: High — adopted, not merely proposed; EU-accession-driven
signals.followup: OPERATOR: retrieve the numbered Bank of Albania Regulation on 'Digital Operational Resilience' (Albanian: Rregullore 'Per qendrueshmerine operacionale dixhitale') and the amended ICT-use regulation from bankofalbania.org/Mbikeqyrja or from Fletorja Zyrtare, to fix the regulation number, the entry-into-force date and the compliance date; then brief OTP Albania and Raiffeisen Albania before their 2027 budget lock.

signals.entity: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo (CBK / BQK)
signals.signal: NON-EU DORA MIRROR ALREADY LIVE AND ABSENT FROM BASELINE. The CBK Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management was approved by the Board of the Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo at its meeting of 29/08/2025, entered into force on 15/09/2025, and — per its final article — 'Financial institutions - FIs are obliged to comply with the requirements of this Regulation, from 1 June 2026.' That compliance date has therefore ALREADY PASSED. It is a 48-page DORA-shaped rulebook applying to banking and non-banking financial institutions (excluding FX-only bureaux and insurance intermediaries), built on the proportionality principle, with dedicated chapters on governance and organisation; strategy, policies and procedures; ICT ASSET AND INFORMATION MANAGEMENT; MANAGEMENT OF THIRD-PARTY SERVICE PROVIDERS; a mandatory ICT BUDGET FORECAST; technology and cyber risk management (risk framework, assessment, monitoring and reporting); project management and acquisition of IT systems; system development life cycle and security by design; testing; patch deployment planning and documentation; access rights authorisation; and cloud services for critical functions requiring board approval. It goes BEYOND the EU minimum on incident timing: institutions must notify and report incidents to the CBK no later than FOUR HOURS after discovery, and the annexed incident form demands hardware manufacturer, software developer and make/model of the affected applications and of the systems on which they run.
signals.source_name: Central Bank of the Republic of Kosovo — 'Regulation on Information Systems and Cyber Risk Management' (English text, PDF)
signals.implies: Kosovo banks (BKT Kosova, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, ProCredit Bank Kosovo, NLB Banka Kosovo, TEB, Banka Ekonomike, Banka per Biznes) are in breach today if they cannot produce an ICT asset register, a third-party provider register, a documented patch process and a 4-hour incident pipeline. The regulation's explicit ICT-budget-forecast requirement is unusually useful: it forces a board-approved ICT spend line. Directly saleable: ATM/device telemetry & monitoring (asset register + make/model/firmware evidence the incident form demands), x-core for multivendor estate visibility, managed/field services for documented patch deployment, and physical ATM security. Kosovo has no firm SEPA date, so this — not payments — is the near-term Kosovo spend trigger.
signals.likelihood: High — already binding since 01/06/2026; supervisory enforcement is the next step
signals.followup: Ask CBK's supervision department whether it has begun on-site inspections against the regulation and whether any enforcement has issued; pitch a Kosovo-wide 'ICT asset register + 4-hour incident evidence' bundle built on device telemetry.

signals.signal: CURRENT NBS ICT RULEBOOK MAPPED FROM THE PRIMARY REGISTER, PLUS ONE GENUINELY NEW 2026 ACT. The NBS's own 'Propisi iz oblasti supervizije informacionih sistema finansijskih institucija' [Regulations on supervision of the information systems of financial institutions] page lists the Serbian ICT/DORA-mirror stack as: (a) 'Odluka o minimalnim standardima upravljanja informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom finansijske institucije' [Decision on minimum standards for managing the ICT system of a financial institution], Sluzbeni glasnik RS 102/2024; (b) 'Odluka o uslovima i nacinu poveravanja aktivnosti u vezi sa informacionim sistemom finansijske institucije trecim licima' [Decision on the conditions and manner of outsourcing information-system activities of a financial institution to third parties], Sl. glasnik RS 100/2023 — Serbia's ICT third-party/outsourcing register equivalent; (c) 'Odluka o tehnickim standardima za pouzdanu autentifikaciju korisnika i zajednickim i bezbednim otvorenim standardima komunikacije' [Decision on technical standards for strong customer authentication and common and secure open standards of communication], Sl. glasnik RS 102/2024; and (d) 'Odluka o uslovima upravljanja informaciono-komunikacionim sistemom pruzaoca usluga povezanih s virtuelnim valutama', Sl. glasnik RS 49/2021. FLAGGED 'NOVO' BY NBS ITSELF: a replacement 'Odluka o uslovima i nacinu utvrdjivanja i provere identiteta fizickog lica koriscenjem sredstava elektronske komunikacije' [Decision on the conditions and manner of establishing and verifying the identity of a natural person using means of electronic communication], Sluzbeni glasnik RS 43/2026, superseding the 2019/2020/2021 version — i.e. Serbia has re-written its remote-identification/video-eKYC rulebook in 2026.
signals.source_name: Narodna banka Srbije — 'Propisi iz oblasti supervizije informacionih sistema finansijskih institucija' (official regulations register)
signals.implies: Two distinct Printec lanes. (1) Decision 100/2023 obliges Serbian banks to document, risk-assess and notify NBS of outsourced information-system activities — Raiffeisen Banka Serbia (x-core) and AIK Banka (NCR recyclers) must carry Printec on that register, so register-grade documentation is a renewal-defence requirement. (2) The NEW Decision 43/2026 on remote identity verification is a direct digital-onboarding/eKYC trigger: it maps to Namirial digital onboarding/eKYC and, where identity proofing runs at a branch device, to bank kiosks and self-service. Serbia's Law on Information Security (non-EU NIS2 mirror) still bites 31/10/2026 alongside this.
signals.likelihood: High — 43/2026 is published and flagged current by NBS
signals.followup: OPERATOR: pull the full text of Odluka 43/2026 from Sluzbeni glasnik RS to establish its application date and whether it permits fully automated (non-video) remote identification — that determines whether the Namirial eKYC configuration sold elsewhere in the footprint is admissible in Serbia. Also confirm whether NBS has issued any ICT rule change since 02/08/2026 (none visible on the register as at 27/08/2026).

signals.country: Austria, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Croatia, Slovenia, Slovakia
signals.signal: FORWARD SIGNAL, NEW. The closing paragraph of ECB letter SSM-2026-0301 (07/07/2026) states that 'other emerging technologies, like the ongoing progress towards practical quantum computing, will have a significant impact on the cybersecurity landscape', that 'the adoption of post-quantum cryptography may involve a longer time frame, but MUST START NOW and necessitates sustained, strategic investment over time', and that 'the ECB will address the emerging risk to traditional encryption methods posed by advances in quantum computing IN A SEPARATE LETTER in due course'. No date is given for that second letter — this is an announced-but-undated supervisory action, not a deadline.
signals.source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — letter SSM-2026-0301, Claudia Buch, 'Addressing AI-enabled cybersecurity threats' (PDF, final paragraph)
signals.implies: A pre-announced second ECB letter on post-quantum cryptography is the clearest medium-term trigger for Thales HSM / PCI refresh across the footprint's SSM banks, and it reaches the ATM and POS estate through PIN-block encryption, key management and remote key loading. Printec should map which Thales HSM units at Alpha Bank, Bank of Cyprus, Erste Croatia, Erste Group and RBI are crypto-agile / PQC-upgradeable BEFORE the letter lands, because the letter will convert a discretionary refresh into a supervised remediation item.
signals.likelihood: Medium-high that the letter issues within 6-12 months; the ECB has committed to it in writing
signals.followup: Monitor bankingsupervision.europa.eu 'Letters to banks' monthly for the PQC letter; in the meantime run a crypto-agility audit of installed Thales HSM estate and ATM/POS key-management chains at SSM-supervised Printec accounts.

signals.signal: WEAKLY SOURCED — TREAT AS A LEAD, NOT A DEADLINE. Montenegrin financial press reports that the CBCG Council adopted a Draft Law on Amendments to the Law on Credit Institutions ('Nacrt zakona o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o kreditnim institucijama') whose stated content includes the digital-operational-resilience requirements of DORA (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 and Directive (EU) 2022/2556), the MiCA crypto-asset framework and CRD6/CRR3 risk-management standards, alongside strengthening of ESG and concentration risk management. NO date of adoption, entry into force or compliance was found at CBCG primary level this run: cbcg.me returned HTTP 404 on its Montenegrin press-centre listing path and the draft law itself was not retrievable. The DORA element for Montenegro is therefore PRESS-TIER ONLY and no date should be relied on.
signals.source_name: Investitor.me / CdM (Montenegrin financial press) reporting on the CBCG Council draft Law on Credit Institutions
signals.implies: If enacted, Montenegro's banks (CKB/OTP Montenegro, NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank Montenegro, Hipotekarna banka, Prva banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Lovcen banka) acquire DORA-shaped ICT-risk, third-party-register and resilience-testing duties on a statutory rather than by-law basis — a bigger and slower instrument than the Albanian or Kosovar regulations, but one that would land in the same 2027-2028 window as the Western Balkans TIPS Clone onboarding. Watch as a 2027 pipeline item for ATM telemetry/monitoring and managed services; do not budget against it yet.
signals.likelihood: Uncertain — draft stage, no published parliamentary timetable found
signals.followup: OPERATOR: retrieve the CBCG Council decision and the Draft Law on Amendments to the Law on Credit Institutions from cbcg.me (the press-centre listing 404s to fetch tools; try the site search or the 'Propisi/Kontrola' PDF directory, which does serve PDFs) and from the Montenegrin Sluzbeni list, to establish whether the DORA chapter survived and what its application date is.
